title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
why_read: A solid empirical benchmark on whether automated machine-learning agents can actually exploit unlabeled data, revealing a concrete and underappreciated bottleneck.
analysis: This work tests whether AI agents that automatically design machine learning pipelines can effectively use semi-supervised learning techniques when labeled data is scarce. The agents were able to write code combining known semi-supervised methods and beat human-engineered baselines in most tested settings. However, the paper identifies a serious weakness: agents often struggle to correctly judge which of their own generated programs are actually good, causing large performance drops. The accompanying benchmark of nearly 17,000 programs is a useful resource for studying this program-selection problem more broadly.
